title: 2020 AMC 10A Problem 17
statement: Define \[ \begin{aligned} P(x)={}&(x-1^2)(x-2^2)\\ &\cdots(x-100^2). \end{aligned} \] How many integers \(n\) are there such that \(P(n)\leq 0?\)

solutions.text:
The polynomial changes sign at each square \(1^2,2^2,\ldots,100^2\), and its leading coefficient is positive. Thus \(P(n)\le0\) for integers in the intervals \([1^2,2^2]\), \([3^2,4^2]\), \(\ldots\), \([99^2,100^2]\).

For odd \(k\), the interval \([k^2,(k+1)^2]\) contains \((k+1)^2-k^2+1=2k+2\) integers. Summing over odd \(k=1,3,\ldots,99\) gives \(2(1+3+\cdots+99)\) \(+2\cdot50=5000+100\) \(=5100\). Thus, E is the correct answer.
